title: Moby-Dick — Loomings (Chapter 1) — Action Spine
adaptation_principle: Preserve the narrator identity hook and compress the chapter’s movement into three concrete choices: go to sea now, choose the common-sailor role, and fix on a whaling voyage. Fold the many rhetorical examples and reasons into the captions over real, present-tense postures; omit tableaux that only illustrate general attraction to water or philosophy.
action_oriented_synopsis: I introduce myself as Ishmael. I decide it is high time to go to sea to cure my spleen. I choose to ship as a simple sailor rather than as a passenger or officer. I resolve on a whaling voyage, welcoming its peril and wonder.

visual_safety_notes: Do not depict whales, phantom figures, mythic scenes, or any imagined tableaux; keep visuals to Ishmael’s present world.
Avoid readable signage, ship names, posters, or street text in backgrounds; include the note No readable text in prompts.
Do not place Ishmael actively aboard ship performing duties; he is deciding and approaching the water, not yet shipped.
Do not show labeled uniforms or ranks (Commodore, Captain, Cook); convey his choice through posture and setting only.
Do not invent specific named locations (e.g., Battery, Manhattan) or show maps; keep the waterfront generic.
Use ships, piers, ropes, and masts as general maritime props only, without logos or legible markings.
